ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There is a circle in the figure, and points S, T, U, V are all on the circle. At point T in the upper left, an inscribed angle is formed by chords TS and TV, labeled beside it as (3x−5)°. At point U above, another inscribed angle is formed by chords US and UV, labeled beside it as (2x+15)°. These two angles both face the same chord SV, that is, they intercept the same arc SV. Reasoning: Inscribed angles subtending the same arc are equal, so ∠STV = ∠SUV. Thus 3x−5 = 2x+15, solving gives x = 20. What is requested is m∠T, namely (3x−5)° = 3(20)−5 = 60−5 = 55°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: points S, T, U, and V lie on the same circle. The marked angle at T is labeled (3x−5)° and is formed by chords TS and TV, so it is ∠STV, the requested angle T. The marked angle at U is labeled (2x+15)° and is formed by chords US and UV, so it is ∠SUV. Both inscribed angles intercept the same chord/arc SV. Use the theorem that inscribed angles intercepting the same arc are congruent: set 3x−5 = 2x+15, solve x = 20, then compute m∠T = 3(20)−5 = 55.
